Week 7, June 17, 2026 in Ocala

Week 7-- The Tortoise and The Wasp

This week was pretty good! Sister Crowther has me listening her her favorite Hank Smith devotionals in the car. It's much better than youth music, so I can't complain. And they're really good, too! For those who don't know, Hank Smith is a famous speaker in our church. He gives really uplifting devotionals, and he has a podcast called Follow Him. I would definitely recommend listening to some of his stuff!

Wednesday, 06/10 We had our weekly lesson with Sister Howard today. She's so sweet and could really use a lot of prayers, so keep her in yours ❤️

We met with our recent convert Clarene. She's currently feuding with one of our other recent converts, so she's going to start attending the later ward's sacrament meetings. Definitely pray for her as well!

Thursday, 06/11 The youth in the stake did a mock MTC, where they learned how to teach the Restoration of Christ's chruch. We were able to demonstrate how to do it, then had them role play teaching it with each other.

Friday, 06/12 We went to Tampa for first transfer training on Friday! My favorite part was when we went outside to do public contacting on the college campus and it started pouring rain-- it was so much fun.

Saturday, 06/13 Story time!

Every Saturday, one of the members of our ward leads a 5k for the members and us missionaries. We usually get a group of 15-20 people, and it's a really fun way to start the morning! Everyone runs the first mile together, and then we split up and run (or walk) at our own pace. Thanks to missionary standards, I have to stay with the group of Sister missionaries. Since they choose to walk and I like to run, I have to run back and forth so I'm always within sight and sound of Sister Crowther.

During the first mile, I feel this little prick inside the sleeve of my shirt. I look down and there's something the size of a large, misshapen goathead entirely underneath my sleeve (keep in mind my sleeves are pretty short, so this was an impressive feat for this unusual goathead). I pick up my sleeve and try to shake it out. I thought it was gone, until I felt another prick a few seconds later slightly below where it was before. At this point, I want whatever this is gone because it's just going to keep poking me and making me sad if I don't. So I reach under my sleeve, take it out and throw it to the side. I feel the texture, and it definitely is not a thorn. I look over as I'm throwing it just in time to see that it was bright yellow and striped. Then I ran a bit faster to get away from the wasp I just threw out of my sleeve.

I rate the experience a 5/10: not very pleasant, but it could have been worse-- I'm very lucky I didn't get stung. However, I would not recommend doing the same thing, as you could have a less desirable result.

Later in the 5k, I saw this cute little tortoise in the path! I turned around and ran yelled at the Sisters to get their attention and inform them it. And you'd never believe what happened next: they started running! Then they stopped to take pictures and recover from that intense few meter jog.

This also meant that I had to run back and forth from the same spot a few times while waiting for them.

On a more spiritual note, we had an amazing lesson with Lovie! She's literally the cutest person ever ❤️ One of the sisters from our ward joined and brought her daughter with her (Lovie has a daughter the same age).

We talked about temples and eternal families and our member shared her testimony so much is was so spiritual and amazing!

Sunday, 06/14 Albert and his wife Andrina made it to church! And Arthur and Jeremiah (brothers that we've been teaching for about a week) came too!

After church, we biked all day. Don't worry, the feels-like temperature was only 104 degrees and the humidity only 57%. I wasn't dying or anything. It was actually all right-- being out in these conditions before my mission would have almost certainly given me a migraine (or at the very least a headache) but I didn't get sick at all! Before I got to Flordia, I worried a lot about having to be out in the intense heat, but so far I've been fine! ✨️ Miracle! ✨️

We had an AMAZING member meal. They made us really good Filipino food. They also served us dessert, which was fresh mangos that they got at Robert is Here (a fruit stand in southern Florida) when they went last week.

We got a referral for Obi (the Wan Kanobi is implied).

Monday, 06/15 I HAD MY FIRST EXCHANGE!! It was so much fun, and we had so many cool experiences! I wish I could put them all here, but you'd be reading this email for DAYS, it would be so long. So I'll put one of them here and you can definitely not skip past it.

We had a member meal! It was this super cute mother and her teenage son. The son had recently (a few months ago) been baptized by his uncle Hank Smith. What was I doing in Idaho when I could've been attending a baptism with Hank Smith in Florida??

Tuesday, 06/16 We had a great doctrinal discussion over zoom with the whole mission Tuesday morning! Unfortunately, we were driving back to Ocala (taking the scenic route, of course) to unexchange, so it was kind of hard to hear. I wasn't driving though, so I could take notes :) President spoke to us a bit, then his bestie BRAD WILCOX shared a message with us. (Brad Wilcox is a church leader who gives especially good spiritual messages-- I'll attatch one to the end of this email)

We had another member meal!! The family that fed us is so funny, and dinner was a blast! It was taco salad, which was AMAZING! For those who don't know me, the only thing that could've made it better was green chile (yum). I've been missing my New Mexican food, but people keep making us food that reminds me of home :)

Wednesday, 06/17 GUYS IT'S P-DAY!!

Spiritual thought (I'm almost done, I promise!): I love this talk by Brad Wilcox because he explains that we all need Christ's Atonement, and that there is no shame in using it. In the devotional he gave us missionaries yesterday, he said something I love. He told us that Christ changes us over time, and that "change is not change without challenge." I love this because it motivates me to keep going, even when I feel like I'm not progressing.

Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness

https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2021/10/35wilcox?lang=eng
